subject: Public-facing data transfer shortcard — concise wording + subprocessor link
messages:
From: Emma Clark <emma.clark@cloudwave.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@cloudwave.com
Date: 2027-05-10T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Quick ask — short public blurb for data transfers/subprocessors

Hi Monica,

We are finalizing our procurement checklist and a few reviewers asked for a one-paragraph, consumer-friendly blurb we can publish that explains: (1) how Redwood moves data internationally, (2) where we can find the current subprocessor list, and (3) what safeguards (e.g. SCCs, encryption in transit) are in place.

Can you share a shortcard or single-paragraph summary that we can drop into our internal vendor registry and share with non-legal stakeholders? Preferably non‑legal language.

Thanks — Emma
Emma Clark
Senior Procurement Manager, CloudWave

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Clark <emma.clark@cloudwave.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — short public blurb for data transfers/subprocessors

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Karthik (privacy/legal) and Laura (product comms).

Karthik: can you confirm the most up-to-date sentence about transfer safeguards we can use publicly (SCCs + contractual and technical safeguards)? Avoid legalese if possible.
Laura: if we can make this ~2–3 short sentences, I’ll send back to Emma with a link to the live subprocessor list.

I attached a first-draft shortcard (very rough).

Monica
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-data-transfer-shortcard-draft-v1.docx

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: se an.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-12T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — short public blurb for data transfers/subprocessors

Monica / Laura —

Suggest the following public-safe phrasing (keeps it high level, accurate, and non-technical):

"Redwood may transfer or process data across international borders to deliver service. We protect customer data with contractual safeguards (including EU Standard Contractual Clauses where required), strong encryption in transit, and access controls. Our current list of subprocessors and transfer safeguards is published and updated here: https://redwood.app/subprocessors/manifest."

Notes:
- "May transfer or process" is intentionally broad and plain.
- Avoid referencing specific certifications in the shortcard; we can call those out elsewhere.
- If CloudWave requires more precise legal formulations, we can provide the DPA excerpt in a follow-up.

Karthik
Head of Privacy & Compliance

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-13T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — short public blurb for data transfers/subprocessors

Thanks — Karthik, that reads well. I edited to make it slightly more customer-facing and dropped the URL into a shorter link for the shortcard:

"To deliver the service, Redwood may process or transfer data across borders. We protect customer data with contractual safeguards (including EU Standard Contractual Clauses where required), strong encryption in transit, and strict access controls. View our current subprocessor list and transfer safeguards: redwood.app/subprocessors."

I also created a one-column shortcard mockup and attached it (same DOCX). Sean — can you quickly confirm that the mention of "encryption in transit" and "access controls" is appropriate to leave as-is for a general audience?

Laura
Senior Product Marketing Manager
